J1.evidence: Arabic: «وأعربه بعضهم بدل اشتمال من الهدي، أي: مسددًا بلوغ الهدي محله». English renders «مسددًا» as 'barring' without the Arabic and without a note — a silent emendation (مسدّدًا normally means 'directing/setting right', not 'barring'). Needs the source word kept and a [Translator's note: …] like the Turkish has.

J2.evidence: Arabic: «وأعربه بعضهم بدل اشتمال من الهدي، أي: مسددًا بلوغ الهدي محله». مسدِّدًا does not mean 'barring'; English renders it 'barring the offering's reaching its place' silently emending the source (as if صادًّا/سادًّا) without a translator's note and without keeping the Arabic. Needs the word kept/translated as written with a [Translator's note: …] on the probable slip (Turkish does this).
